title: あげる / くれる / もらう (giving and receiving objects)
meaning: あげる = I/someone gives to another (outward); くれる = someone gives to me / my in-group (inward); もらう = receive.
simpleExplanation: Japanese has three verbs for giving and receiving, and the choice depends on direction. あげる = give (from me or someone to another person; the thing moves away from the speaker). くれる = give (to me or my family or group; the thing moves toward the speaker). もらう = receive. So 友達が私に本をくれた and 私は友達に本をもらった describe the same event from two sides. Each verb has polite and humble versions for talking to superiors.
whenUsed: Presents, favours, lending and borrowing in daily life; describing who gave what to whom. くれる is only for things that come to the speaker's side. Politeness: さしあげる (I give to a superior), くださる (a superior gives me), いただく (I receive from a superior).
formation: A は B に N を あげる: I/someone give to another person
B は (私に) N を くれる: someone gives to me / my group
私は B に / B から N を もらう: I receive from someone
Levels: さしあげる / あげる / やる; くださる / くれる; いただく / もらう

diagram.translation: My friend gave me a present. (Same event with もらう: 私は友達にプレゼントをもらいました.)

examples.ja: 私は友達に本をあげました。
examples.reading: わたしは ともだちに ほんを あげました。
examples.en: I gave my friend a book.
examples.note: あげる: the speaker gives outward; receiver takes に.

examples.ja: 友達が私にプレゼントをくれました。
examples.reading: ともだちが わたしに プレゼントを くれました。
examples.en: My friend gave me a present.
examples.note: くれる: the giver is the subject, the speaker receives.

examples.ja: 私は先生に辞書をもらいました。
examples.reading: わたしは せんせいに じしょを もらいました。
examples.en: I received a dictionary from my teacher.
examples.note: もらう: the speaker is the subject and receives; the giver takes に (or から).

examples.ja: 母の日に、母に花をあげました。
examples.reading: ははのひに、ははに はなを あげました。
examples.en: I gave my mother flowers on Mother's Day.
examples.note: あげる: giving from the speaker to someone else, even family.

examples.ja: 先生が私にとてもいい辞書をくださいました。
examples.reading: せんせいが わたしに とても いい じしょを くださいました。
examples.en: My teacher gave me a really good dictionary.
examples.note: くださる is the respectful form of くれる, used because the giver is a teacher.

similarGrammar.difference: The same directions apply to actions: てあげる = do for someone (outward).
てくれる = someone does something for me (inward).
てもらう = I have someone do something for me; the doer takes に.

commonMistakes.wrong: 先生は私にプレゼントをあげました。
commonMistakes.right: 先生は私にプレゼントをくださいました。
commonMistakes.why: When the receiver is the speaker, the verb must be くれる / くださる, never あげる.

commonMistakes.wrong: 私は友達がプレゼントをもらいました。
commonMistakes.right: 私は友達にプレゼントをもらいました。
commonMistakes.why: With もらう the giver takes に or から, not が.

commonMistakes.wrong: 私は先生に本をさしあげてもらいました。
commonMistakes.right: 私は先生に本をいただきました。
commonMistakes.why: Receiving from a superior is いただく. Do not mix humble giving with receiving.

usageNotes: Family members count as the speaker's side: 隣の人が弟にお菓子をくれた is correct because the receiver (my younger brother) is closer to me than the giver. When unsure, keep the receiver as 私.
やる is used for giving to pets, plants and much younger people: 犬にえさをやる. Some speakers use あげる here too.
から instead of に is required when the giver is an organisation: 会社から記念品をもらった.
jlptTips: First find the receiver. If it is 私 or my family, the verb is くれる (giver が) or もらう (giver に). If the receiver is someone else and the giver is 私, use あげる.
Check the particle on the person: X が … くれる vs X に … もらう. Questions often keep the verb and blank the particle, or keep the particle and blank the verb.
